summary: Contact Carlos Ruiz and Sarah Kim directly about EV and hybrid parts sourcing as they progress through retraining. Simultaneously, draft a simple one-page commercial accounts capability sheet for Howard's Parts — a concise document that can be handed or emailed to any B2B prospect covering product lines, lead times, and minimum order terms. Keep costs low this tick — no sample orders, no new outreach spend. The savings drop from tick 5 was planned, but I need to let those seeds germinate without burning more capital.
reasoning: The sector index at 79 and the wave of layoffs at the dealership confirm what I already suspected: the contraction is real and accelerating. Patricia laid off people she knew. Rick is scrambling. Jake is fighting to stay categorized as essential. I am watching the same forces hit the retail auto ecosystem from my own angle — fewer DIY customers, lower foot traffic, a market that is shifting under me. The RoboRide and municipality follow-ups have been made. I spent real money on the brake consumable sample. I cannot keep spending into silence. This tick I consolidate: deepen the relationships that have the best chance of converting (Carlos and Sarah, who are actively transitioning toward EV work and will need a reliable local parts source), and build a professional-grade capability document so that when RoboRide or the municipality asks 'what can you actually supply us?' I have something concrete to hand them. No new cold outreach spend this tick. No heroics. Steady.

actions.description: Call Carlos Ruiz directly — a short, professional call, not a sales pitch. Reference the earlier conversation about EV parts sourcing. Ask specifically: now that his EV retraining is progressing, what components is he expecting to need that his current suppliers are slow on? High-voltage safety gear? ADAS calibration tools? Battery management system connectors? I want a specific list, not a general conversation. I tell him I am building out my EV/hybrid inventory line and I want his shop to have a reliable local source when the time comes. No obligation. Just alignment.
actions.expected_outcome: Strengthen the relationship with Carlos as he transitions toward EV work. Get specific inventory intelligence. Plant Howard's Parts as the go-to local supplier for EV-related parts as that segment grows.

actions.description: Send Sarah Kim a brief, low-pressure message — text or a quick call. I know she is also pursuing EV training based on what I've heard. I introduce myself properly if needed and mention that I stocked up on EV and hybrid consumables recently and would be happy to be her first call when she needs parts for that kind of work. Keep it short. I am not pitching hard — I am making myself easy to remember when the moment arrives.
actions.expected_outcome: Establish a working relationship with Sarah Kim before she has cemented supplier habits for EV work. Low cost, potentially high value as EV service volume grows.

actions.description: Draft a one-page commercial accounts capability sheet for Howard's Parts. One page. Professional. It covers: (1) Product lines available — brake hardware, sensors, lubricants, safety consumables, EV/hybrid components, import vehicle specialty parts; (2) Typical lead times for common SKUs vs. special order; (3) Minimum order quantities for commercial accounts; (4) Contact information and preferred ordering method. This document exists so that when RoboRide, the municipality, or any commercial prospect asks 'what exactly can you supply?' I have something concrete in hand. Digital and printable.
actions.expected_outcome: A reusable sales tool that professionalizes the commercial account pitch and removes ambiguity from B2B conversations. No spend required — this is time and discipline.

financial_impact.notes: Tick 5 cost $689 in sample consumables. That was an intentional investment. This tick I hold the line on spending and let those investments do their work. No new cash outflows planned.

emotional_state: Disciplined and watchful. The layoffs at the dealership are a gut-check. Patricia laying off people she knew personally — that is the kind of thing that reminds you the transition is not abstract. I have two kids and a mortgage and a store that is adapting but not yet transformed. I am not panicking. But I am not comfortable either, and I do not want to be. Comfort is what kept me too patient for too long.
